info.title: Juiced API
info.description: API for submitting pings and leads to Juiced. Build on the v1 endpoints under `/v1`. The unversioned `/ping` and `/leads` endpoints are the frozen legacy contract and are deprecated.

post.description:
Submits partial lead data to check for matching bids before sending the full lead. Use it to see pricing and availability before you commit to a full lead submission.

The response depends on your source type.
- **Vendor sources** receive a single `price`, never the bids behind it.
- **Every other source** receives the matching `bids`, each with the buyer's name for TCPA consent.

Every ping that passes validation returns `200`, whatever its `status`. Keep the returned `id` and send it as `ping_id` when you post the lead.

200.description: Ping evaluated. Check `data.status` for the outcome.

Matched with no bidder (marketplace or C.summary: Matched with no bidder (marketplace or Club)

get.description:
Lists the leads in your account, newest first, 50 at a time. Filter by the customer or partner who bought them, their status, or when they came in. Test leads are left out unless you send `include_test=true`.

No contact details are returned. Get those with [Get Lead Details](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/leads-details).

Authenticates with an API key, not a source's credentials. Requires the `leads:read` ability.

parameters.description: Only leads this customer bought, including ones they returned. Archived customers work too.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: Only leads sold to this partner, including ones they returned. Archived partners work too.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Only leads created at or after this time, as ISO 8601 with any offset, like `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z` or `2026-11-01T00:00:00-05:00`.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Only leads created before this time, as ISO 8601 with any offset. It must be later than `created_after`.

post.description:
Submits a complete lead for processing. The lead is validated, checked for duplicates, matched to a lead type, and distributed to a buyer (or placed in the marketplace or Club).

If you pinged first, include the ping's `id` as `ping_id`. You can also echo the `bids[].id` you chose as `bid_id`. It's checked, but it doesn't change who gets the lead.

Send a `transaction_id` so a retry can never create a second lead. One `transaction_id` is one lead on either API version.

post.description:
Creates a customer. Only `name` and `email` are required. With `send_invite`, the customer is emailed an invite to set up their portal login.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so a retry can never create a second customer.

Requires the `customers:write` ability.

post.description:
Archives the customer and their bids, as archiving in Juiced does. An archived customer stops receiving leads, and their email can be used for a new customer.

Archiving a customer who is already archived changes nothing and returns them, so a retry is safe.

Requires the `customers:write` ability.

Brings an archived customer back, as reactivating in Juiced does. Their bids come back paused, so they don't receive leads until the bids are turned back on.

Reactivating a customer who isn't archived changes nothing and returns them, so a retry is safe.

Requires the `customers:write` ability.

post.description:
**Deprecated.** This is the frozen legacy contract. Build new integrations on [`POST /v1/ping`](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/ping). Every response carries a `Deprecation` header and a `Link` header pointing to the v1 endpoint.

The response has one of two shapes.
- **Bids** has `ping_id`, `message` and `bids`. Non-vendor sources get it when the ping went through matching, and for test-mode zips.
- **Price** has `message`, `price` and `ping_id`. Vendor sources always get it, and so does any ping answered before matching (duplicate, quota reached, or rejected).

PartnerIdHeader.name: X-Partner-Id
PartnerIdHeader.description: Public ID of the partner you're pinging on behalf of. The ping is recorded against that partner when the partner is linked to the source whose credentials you use. Optional but recommended for any partner-mediated integration.

XRequestId.description: Unique ID for this request, sent on every v1 response (errors included). Quote it when contacting support.

Deprecation.description: Marks the legacy endpoint as deprecated (RFC 9745). The value is `@` followed by the Unix timestamp of the deprecation date.

SuccessorLink.description: Points to the v1 endpoint that replaces this one.

Basic Auth.description: Use your source's API key as the username and API secret as the password. Base64 encode the credentials in the format `api_key:api_secret`.

Bearer Token.description: Use a bearer token generated for your source.

API Key.description: An API key from **Configure → API Keys** (it starts with `jz_live_`), sent as a bearer token. See [API Keys](/api-reference/api-keys).

zip.description: Postal code. Must be valid for your account's operating countries. With the source in test mode, zips `00001` to `00005` return fixed outcomes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional fields as configured for your source and lead category. Only fields marked required for ping must be sent.

transaction_id.description: Your own ID for this lead, such as an order or lead number. A retry with the same `transaction_id` and payload returns the original response instead of creating a second lead. Numbers are accepted and treated as strings.

ping_id.description: The `id` returned by `POST /v1/ping`. Links this lead to the ping's match and pricing. A legacy ping UUID is rejected.

bid_id.description: Any `bids[].id` returned by `POST /v1/ping` for your account. It is checked but doesn't change who gets the lead.

zip.description: Postal code. Must be valid for your account's operating countries. With the source in test mode, zips `00001` to `00005` return fixed outcomes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional fields as configured for your source and lead category.

id.description: The ping's ID. Send it as `ping_id` when you post the lead.

status.description: How the ping was answered. `matched` means a buyer (or the marketplace or Club) will take the lead. `no_match` means nobody will, including when the source has reached a lead quota. `duplicate` means it matched a duplicate check. `rejected` means it was refused before matching.

price.description: Vendor sources only. The price offered for the lead, in dollars. `0` when there's no match.

bids.description: Every source except vendors. The bids behind the answer. Empty when there's no match.

reason.description: Only on a ping rejected by the distribution loop guard, because the ping already passed through this account or exceeded the hop limit.

id.description: The bid's ID. It's a `bid_…` for a customer bid, the partner's `prt_…` for a partner, or the ping's own `ping_…` when the match has no bidder behind it (marketplace or Club). Echo it as `bid_id` when you post the lead.

price.description: Price offered for the lead, in dollars.

tcpa_name.description: Buyer name to use in TCPA consent language.

customer_id.description: Present when a customer placed the bid. The customer's public ID.

partner_id.description: Present when a partner made the offer. The partner's public ID.

status.description: The outcome, decided by the source's status response mapping. By default, `accepted` covers leads that were assigned, posted to a partner, placed on the marketplace or parked in the Club; `rejected` covers Unassigned, Audit and Uncategorized leads; `duplicate` covers duplicates.

price.description: What the source earns for the lead, in dollars. Always `0` unless `status` is `accepted`.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Branch on this, not on `message`.

errors.description: Only with `validation_failed`. Messages keyed by field.

lead_id.description: Only with `idempotency_version_mismatch`. The lead the `transaction_id` already created.

bid.description: Only when a customer already has an active bid on that lead type and location. That bid's ID, so you can change it instead.

paused.description: Whether the customer is paused and gets no leads.

can_access_bidding.description: Whether the customer can place bids.

can_access_club.description: Whether the customer can join the Club.

balance.description: Available balance in dollars, after funds held for pending pings.

daily_budget.description: Most spent a day, in dollars.

weekly_budget.description: Most spent a week, in dollars.

monthly_budget.description: Most spent a month, in dollars.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page.

name.description: The customer's business or display name.

email.description: Must include a domain with a TLD. Unique across your active customers. An archived customer's email can be used again.

phone.description: A US, Canadian, Australian or Latvian phone number.

zip.description: Checked against `country`, which is required with it.

daily_lead_cap.description: Most leads a day. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise.

weekly_lead_cap.description: Most leads a week. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise.

monthly_lead_cap.description: Most leads a month. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise.

daily_budget.description: Most spent a day, in dollars. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise.

weekly_budget.description: Most spent a week, in dollars. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise.

monthly_budget.description: Most spent a month, in dollars. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise.

send_invite.description: Email the customer an invite to set up their portal login.

state.description: State, province or region abbreviation, like `TX`.

customer.description: The customer the lead was sold to, or `null` when it went to a partner. Exactly one of `customer` and `partner` is set.

partner.description: The partner the lead was sold to, or `null` when it went to a customer. Exactly one of `customer` and `partner` is set.

price.description: What this buyer, customer or partner, paid for the lead, in dollars.

assigned_at.description: When the lead was assigned to this buyer.

returned_at.description: When this buyer returned the lead. `null` unless they returned it.

status.description: The lead's status. `club` is a lead in your Club and `returned` is a lead its buyer returned. When a lead was sold more than once, read `assignments` for each sale.

lead_type.description: The lead type's ID, or `null` when the lead didn't match a lead type.

source.description: The ID of the source that sent the lead.

price.description: What the lead sold for, in dollars, which is its first sale, whether to a customer or a partner. Each buyer's own price is in `assignments`.

test.description: Whether the lead is test data.

assignments.description: One entry for each sale, to a customer or a partner, oldest first, including sales that were returned. A partner send that's still in progress isn't listed until it's delivered.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page.

fields.description: The lead's deliverable fields, keyed by field title, with the same keys and values a v1 customer webhook sends for the lead. An empty object when the lead has none.

type.description: `credit` added to the balance and `debit` took from it.

event.description: What produced the transaction. See [List Transactions](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/transactions-list) for what each one means.

amount.description: In dollars. Positive for a credit, negative for a debit.

balance.description: The customer's wallet balance right after this transaction, in dollars, before funds held for pending pings. It's the same in the transaction history and in the response to [Add or Remove Funds](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/transactions-create).

description.description: What the transaction was for. Your own description on credits and debits you make, otherwise a short label for the event, like `Lead charge` or `Payment`.

lead.description: The lead's ID when the transaction is for a lead, such as a `lead_charge` or `lead_refund`.

receipt_url.description: A link to the payment's receipt. Only on `customer_payment`, `manual_credit` and `auto_recharge`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page.

type.description: `credit` adds to the customer's balance and `debit` takes from it.

amount.description: In dollars, with at most 2 decimal places. Always positive, since `type` sets the direction. A debit can't be more than the customer's balance.

description.description: What the funds are for, like `Invoice 1042 paid`. The customer sees it on their transactions.

receipt_url.description: Credits only. A link to the receipt in your own billing system. Sending one with a debit is refused.

customer.description: The customer who placed the bid.

lead_type.description: The lead type the bid is on.

scope.description: How wide the bid reaches, set by the depth of its location.

amount.description: What the customer bids for a lead, in dollars.

minimum.description: The lead type's minimum bid at this scope, in dollars. `null` when the lead type has no bidding set up at this scope.

below_minimum.description: Whether `amount` is under `minimum`. That's allowed, as it is in Juiced.

daily_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a day.

weekly_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a week.

monthly_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a month.

daily_budget.description: Most this bid spends a day, in dollars.

weekly_budget.description: Most this bid spends a week, in dollars.

monthly_budget.description: Most this bid spends a month, in dollars.

status.description: The bid's status, as Juiced shows it. See [Display status](/features/bidding#display-status). It doesn't cover the customer's own account, so check `can_receive_leads` too.

can_receive_leads.description: Whether the bid can win leads right now. It runs the same check distribution does.

blocked_by.description: Every reason the bid can't receive leads right now, bid-level reasons first. Empty when `can_receive_leads` is `true`. See [Get a Bid](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/bids-get) for what each code means.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page.

BidLocationInputV1.title: Bid Location
BidLocationInputV1.description: Where the bid applies. Its depth sets the scope. `country` alone is a nationwide bid, adding `state` makes a state bid, and adding `county_fips` makes a county bid.

country.description: Two-letter code of one of your operating countries, like `US`.

state.description: The state, province or region abbreviation, like `TX`. It must be in `country`.

county_fips.description: A US county's 5-digit FIPS code, like `48201`. County bids are US only. `state` is optional with it, but must be the county's state when you send it.

lead_type.description: The lead type's ID, from [List Lead Types](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/lead-types-list). Bidding must be turned on for it at the location's scope.

amount.description: What the customer bids for a lead, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. It can be below the lead type's minimum, which `below_minimum` flags.

daily_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a day. Only accepted when the bid daily lead cap is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

weekly_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a week. Only accepted when the bid weekly lead cap is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

monthly_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a month. Only accepted when the bid monthly lead cap is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

daily_budget.description: Most this bid spends a day, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. Only accepted when the bid daily budget is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

weekly_budget.description: Most this bid spends a week, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. Only accepted when the bid weekly budget is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

monthly_budget.description: Most this bid spends a month, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. Only accepted when the bid monthly budget is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

BidUpdateRequestV1.title: Bid Update Request
BidUpdateRequestV1.description: Send only the fields you want to change.

lead_type.description: Move the bid to another lead type. Bidding must be turned on for it at the bid's scope.

amount.description: What the customer bids for a lead, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places.

daily_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a day. Only accepted when the bid daily lead cap is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

weekly_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a week. Only accepted when the bid weekly lead cap is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

monthly_lead_cap.description: Most leads this bid gets a month. Only accepted when the bid monthly lead cap is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

daily_budget.description: Most this bid spends a day, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. Only accepted when the bid daily budget is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

weekly_budget.description: Most this bid spends a week, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. Only accepted when the bid weekly budget is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

monthly_budget.description: Most this bid spends a month, in dollars with at most 2 decimal places. Only accepted when the bid monthly budget is turned on in **Configure → Bidding**, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove it.

paused.description: `true` pauses the bid and `false` turns it back on.

id.description: The lead type's public ID. Send it as `lead_type` when you create a bid.

bidding.description: The scopes bids can be placed at, with each one's minimum. Empty when bidding isn't turned on for the lead type.

minimum.description: The minimum bid at this scope, in dollars.

next_cursor.description: Always `null`. Every lead type comes back in one page.

CustomerUpdateRequestV1.description: Send only the fields to change. Fields you leave out keep their current values. Any other field, such as auto-recharge settings, is ignored.

name.description: The customer's business or display name.

email.description: Must include a domain with a TLD. Unique across your active customers, so an email another active customer uses is refused with `validation_failed`.

phone.description: A US, Canadian, Australian or Latvian phone number. Send `null` to clear it.

address.description: Once set, it can be changed but not cleared.

city.description: Once set, it can be changed but not cleared.

state.description: Once set, it can be changed but not cleared.

zip.description: Checked against `country`, or the customer's stored country when `country` isn't sent. Once set, it can be changed but not cleared.

country.description: Required with `state` or `zip` when the customer has no country yet. Once set, it can be changed but not cleared.

paused.description: Pausing stops the customer receiving leads, exactly as pausing them in Juiced does. Send `false` to unpause.

daily_lead_cap.description: Most leads a day. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove the limit.

weekly_lead_cap.description: Most leads a week. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove the limit.

monthly_lead_cap.description: Most leads a month. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove the limit.

daily_budget.description: Most spent a day, in dollars. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove the limit.

weekly_budget.description: Most spent a week, in dollars. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove the limit.

monthly_budget.description: Most spent a month, in dollars. Accepted only when the matching cap or budget is turned on in your account settings, and ignored otherwise. Send `null` to remove the limit.

transaction_id.description: Your own ID for this lead, such as an order or lead number. A retry with the same `transaction_id` and payload returns the original response instead of creating a second lead. Numbers are accepted and treated as strings.

ping_id.description: The `ping_id` returned by the ping (a UUID), or the ping's `ping_…` public ID.

bid_id.description: A bid `id` from the ping response. It must be a UUID, so a partner's numeric bid `id` can't be echoed. It doesn't change who gets the lead.

zip.description: Postal code. Must be valid for your account's operating countries. With the source in test mode, zips `00001` to `00005` return fixed outcomes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional fields as configured for your source and lead category.

LegacyPingResponseBids.title: Bids
LegacyPingResponseBids.description: Non-vendor sources, when the ping went through matching or used a test-mode zip.

ping_id.description: The ping's ID. Send it as `ping_id` when you post the lead.

message.description: Result of the ping. `Duplicate` and `Rejected` only appear here for test-mode zips.

bids.description: Bids for this lead. Empty when there's no match.

LegacyPingResponsePrice.title: Price
LegacyPingResponsePrice.description: Vendor sources, and any ping answered before matching (duplicate, quota reached, or rejected).

message.description: Result of the ping. A source over its lead quota gets `No match found`.

price.description: Price offered for the lead, in dollars. `0` unless matched.

ping_id.description: The ping's ID. Send it as `ping_id` when you post the lead.

reason.description: Only on a ping rejected by the distribution loop guard.

id.description: The bid's UUID for a customer bid, the partner's numeric ID for a partner, or the ping's UUID when the match has no bidder behind it (marketplace or Club).

price.description: Price offered for the lead, in dollars.

tcpa_name.description: Buyer name to use in TCPA consent language.

customer_id.description: Present when a customer placed the bid.

partner_id.description: Present when a partner made the offer.

lead_uuid.description: Internal UUID for the lead. Prefer `lead_public_id`.

status.description: The outcome, decided by the source's status response mapping. By default, `success` covers leads that were assigned, posted to a partner, placed on the marketplace or parked in the Club; `rejected` covers Unassigned, Audit and Uncategorized leads; `duplicate` covers duplicates.

price.description: What the source earns for the lead, in dollars. Always `0` unless `status` is `success`.

message.description: The first error, followed by a count of any others.
message.example: The email field must be a valid email address. (and 1 more error)

email: The email field must be a valid email address.

error.example: Lead data does not match ping data

UnauthenticatedV1.description: Credentials are missing or invalid. Every authentication failure returns the same error.

error.message: Missing or invalid API credentials. Send a bearer token or Basic credentials for an active source.
Too many requests. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.

ServerErrorV1.description: Something went wrong on our side. Quote the `X-Request-Id` header when contacting support.

error.message: An unexpected error occurred. Quote the X-Request-Id header when contacting support.

ApiKeyUnauthenticatedV1.description: The API key is missing, unknown, revoked or expired.

error.message: Missing or invalid API key. Send an active jz_live_ key as a bearer token.

ApiKeyForbiddenV1.description: The key lacks the ability this endpoint needs, your plan doesn't include the API, or your account is locked for an unpaid subscription.

error.message: This API key does not have the customers:write ability.
The API is not included in your plan. Upgrade to a paid plan to use it.
This workspace is locked until its subscription is paid.

LegacyUnauthorized.description: Credentials are missing or invalid. A rejected bearer token returns `Unauthenticated.`; anything else returns `Unauthorized`.

Missing header or wrong Basic credential.summary: Missing header or wrong Basic credentials
